batchName: Late Republic: Spartacus and Pompey (78-63 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: Spartacus and Pompey (78-63 BCE)

questions.question: What was decimation, the ancient punishment Crassus revived?
options: Executing one soldier in ten by lot
Cutting soldiers' pay by a tenth
questions.explanation: In decimation, one soldier in every ten was chosen by lot and executed. Crassus' men learned he was more dangerous to them than the enemy.
questions.sourceQuote: He revived decimation (*decimatio*), an ancient punishment in which one soldier in every ten was chosen by lot and executed.

questions.question: Why do we have no record, in their own words, of what Spartacus' rebels wanted?
options: Their records were lost at sea
No rebel ever wrote their aims down
questions.explanation: Because the revolt failed, no rebel recorded its aims. Everything we know comes from Roman and Greek writers, who disagree with each other.
questions.sourceQuote: Because the revolt failed, no rebel ever wrote down what Spartacus and his followers hoped to achieve.

questions.question: The Servile Wars took their name from the Latin word for what?
questions.explanation: 'Servile' comes from servus, Latin for slave. The first two Servile Wars broke out on Sicily in 135 and 104 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: These became known as the First and Second Servile Wars, from the Latin word for slave (*servus*).

questions.question: By spring 72 BC, where was Spartacus' slave army heading?
questions.explanation: The rebels marched north towards Cisalpine Gaul, the Roman province below the Alps. The alarmed Senate sent both consuls against them.
questions.sourceQuote: By spring 72 BC, Spartacus' slave army was heading north towards Cisalpine Gaul, the Roman province in Italy's far north below the Alps.

questions.question: Films often show Spartacus' rebels fighting to abolish slavery. What do the ancient writers say about this?
options: They say Roman citizenship was the aim
They say abolishing slavery was the aim
None says that was their goal
They say freeing gladiators was the aim
questions.explanation: No ancient writer claims the rebels wanted to end slavery, and nothing their leaders did seems aimed at it. It is not even certain Spartacus was the sole commander.
questions.sourceQuote: No ancient writer says this was their goal, and nothing the leaders did seems aimed at ending slavery as such.

questions.question: What earned the young Pompey the nickname 'teenage butcher'?
options: Burning a rebel town in Sicily
questions.explanation: While hunting the dictator's enemies in Sicily and North Africa, Pompey executed a captured former consul. The Latin nickname was adulescentulus carnifex.
questions.sourceQuote: His execution of a captured former consul earned him the nickname "teenage butcher" (*adulescentulus carnifex*).

questions.question: What animal did the bitter Lucullus compare Pompey to, for feeding on other men's work?
questions.explanation: Lucullus called Pompey a vulture, also mocking his claim to have finished off Spartacus, whom Crassus had really beaten.
questions.sourceQuote: The bitter Lucullus, the general he replaced, called Pompey a vulture who fed on other men's work, mocking his claim to have finished off Spartacus as well.

questions.question: Where were about 6,000 captured survivors of Spartacus' army crucified?
questions.explanation: The prisoners were crucified along the Appian Way, the great road linking Rome to Capua, where the revolt had begun.
questions.sourceQuote: About 6,000 captured survivors were crucified along the Appian Way (*Via Appia*), the great road from Rome to Capua.

questions.question: According to the Greek biographer, what did the Senate do with the two consuls of 72 BC?
questions.explanation: The two main ancient accounts tell the campaign differently, but both have the consuls beaten by Spartacus. Only a breakaway rebel band near Mount Garganus had been destroyed.
questions.sourceQuote: He adds that the Senate then recalled both consuls.

questions.question: To whom did the Senate turn in 71 BC to defeat Spartacus' army?
questions.explanation: The desperate Senate gave command to Crassus, an immensely rich politician. He received eight legions, perhaps 32,000 to 48,000 trained soldiers.
questions.sourceQuote: By 71 BC the Senate turned in desperation to Crassus, the immensely rich politician who now took on the slave army.
